name: Membership and Equivalence Queries Complexity
definition: The **Membership and Equivalence Queries Complexity** of $\mathcal{H}$ is the minimum worst-case number of queries needed to identify an unknown target in $\mathcal{H}$ when the learner may use membership queries and arbitrary equivalence queries.
graph_summary: Minimum worst-case number of membership or arbitrary equivalence queries needed to identify the target.
origin_references: Membership and equivalence queries in the exact query-learning model are introduced in \cite{angluin1988queries}.

monotonic.proof: Any membership-and-arbitrary-equivalence-query strategy that identifies every target in $\mathcal H$ also identifies every target in a subfamily $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$, with the same worst-case number of queries.

c_monotonic.proof: For a fibre, membership labels on fixed coordinates are known.  For an arbitrary equivalence hypothesis, first replace its fixed-coordinate values by the prescribed fibre labels; any counterexample in the remaining coordinates is a valid counterexample to the restricted hypothesis.  This simulates a strategy for the original class with no more queries.
